text: The system shall accept the declaration of a connection, a change to a declared connection and the removal of a declared connection.
rationale: REQ-PL-031 and DEC-125.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of a connection that does not state the service, the account, the scopes of access, and whether the account can commit funds or communicate with a third party in the name of the user.
rationale: DEC-125. The scopes are what REQ-EX-013 refuses a credential against, and the account is what the credential is for. Whether a connection is metered is not stated, because REQ-EX-006 makes it metered until the user answers. REQ-EX-026 refuses against the last.

text: The system shall accept the declaration of a connection, a change to a connection and the removal of a connection from an agent only.
rationale: REQ-PL-028. REQ-AC-004 states the same for an act.

text: The system shall hold, with each declared connection, the writer that declared it and the time of the declaration.
rationale: REQ-PL-029. REQ-AC-005 states the same for an act.

text: The system shall not accept the removal of a connection until the platform records an affirmative answer to a request that states that removal.
rationale: DEC-125 adds the removal of a connection to the acts that DEC-113 names. The user wants to answer it, as for the removal of data.

text: The system shall treat a connection as metered unless the platform records an affirmative answer to a request that states that the connection is not metered.
rationale: DEC-165. An agent that states a paid service as not metered escapes the limit of REQ-EX-024, and a weaker gate needs the user (DEC-113). The shape of DEC-109.

text: The system shall give the caller, with each refusal of an act that has no affirmative answer of the user, that the act needs an affirmative answer of the user.
rationale: DEC-104. REQ-IN-034 states the same in Ingestion. Without it the caller does not learn that the act needs an answer.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of a connection, a change to it and its removal from a caller whose position does not admit the act.
rationale: DEC-019 and DEC-123. A position bounds which agent may ask the user for a connection, which keeps the user from requests that no work needs (DEC-125).

text: The system shall accept a call of a caller to an act that it holds, and a released gated unit whose act it holds, only from Actuation, with the caller or the raiser that Actuation states.
rationale: DEC-111 and DEC-123. REQ-IN-031 states the same in Ingestion.

text: The system shall give Actuation the result of each call and each released gated unit that Actuation carried to it.
rationale: DEC-111. REQ-IN-032 states the same in Ingestion.

text: The system shall refuse a released gated unit whose act the position of its raiser does not admit.
rationale: DEC-048: a yes is not a change to what a position admits. REQ-IN-033 states the same in Ingestion.

text: The system shall accept the credential of a connection only from the user through Interaction, or from the service in answer to a consent that the system started for that connection.
rationale: DEC-125. A key that the user gives reaches the system through Interaction, which identifies the user (REQ-IA-035). A consent at a service returns through the browser of the user, and the system accepts it only with the value that it put in the request for that consent, so an answer that the system did not ask for is refused. A credential that an agent holds is in its context, in the calls to its model and in the record of its exchanges.

text: The system shall not hold a credential that gives access which no declared connection states.
rationale: RSK-EX-008 and DEC-125. The user consents to what the service shows, and a consent can be wider than the connection that an agent declared or can have no connection at all. The first draft held the case of no connection as a second row. A connection that is changed to fewer scopes leaves the credential that the system holds wider than it, so the row states what the system holds and not only what it accepts.

text: The system shall renew each credential before it stops being valid, where the service permits a renewal.
rationale: A credential that expires stops each acquisition and each act that uses it. A key that the service does not renew is found by REQ-EX-018.

text: When a connection is removed, the system shall revoke its credential at the service where the service accepts a revocation, and shall otherwise raise the work to revoke it.
rationale: RSK-EX-002. A credential that is only removed from the host still works at the service. Most services that use OAuth accept a revocation, and a key is often revoked only by a person at the service.

text: The system shall not give a credential to another system, including in the record of a call.
rationale: RSK-EX-004 and DEC-161. A session that an agent drives is signed in by this system (REQ-EX-017), and the agent does not read the credential.

text: The system shall sign in a session that an agent drives as a sequence of steps with the credential of its connection.
rationale: DEC-127. The user wants a session signed in without an act of the user. A second factor that the service asks for is an act of the user (DEC-097).

text: The system shall raise work when a declared connection has no valid credential.
rationale: DEC-168, DEC-012 and OPN-031. A connection that is new has no credential yet, and a credential that stops being valid leaves the connection with none, so one row raises the work for both. The consent is an act of the user (DEC-097), so an agent tells the user.

text: The system shall give Work and Coordination the event that a declared connection that had no valid credential has one.
rationale: DEC-093 has one reporter for each kind of event, and a unit of work can wait on this one, for a new connection as for a credential that stopped being valid (REQ-EX-018). OPN-076.

text: The system shall accept a call to an external service only from Actuation, Ingestion, Interaction, Agent Runtime and State Custody.
rationale: DEC-123 and OPN-080. This system checks no authority over a call that it carries, so REQ-PL-014 holds only while no other system reaches it. Actuation gives each act on the outside world (REQ-AC-019), Ingestion a call for each acquisition that names the connection of the source (DEC-129, OPN-025), Interaction a message through a push service, and Agent Runtime a call to a model (DEC-161, DEC-140). The first draft held one row to accept from each caller and one to refuse the rest, in the shape of REQ-IN-031 it is one. State Custody gives a call to a model for an embedding, and Ingestion and Interaction also give calls to a model that does not generate (DEC-154).

text: The system shall give the caller of each call the result of that call, or that the call returned no result.
rationale: REQ-EX-022 does not repeat a call, so the caller must learn that it returned no result and decide (REQ-AC-024).

text: The system shall not repeat a call.
rationale: RSK-EX-009 and DEC-129. A call that returned no result may have had its effect, and the caller decides. A repeat that the service offers is the service's.

text: The system shall accept from Agent Definition the position that speaks to the user and the position that receives a unit of work that names no agent.
rationale: DEC-165 keeps the calls to a model of the agents that hold these positions after the limit.

text: The system shall refuse each call to a metered connection when the metered cost of the month reaches TBD, apart from each call that Interaction gives and each call to a model of an agent that holds the position that speaks to the user or the position that receives a unit of work that names no agent.
rationale: DEC-165. Interaction gives its messages and its calls to a model for speech. The value is a part of USD 50 that the fixed costs do not use, and is not yet known.

text: The system shall report when it starts to refuse calls under the limit of the month.
rationale: RSK-EX-015. DEC-165 and DEC-162: no act lifts the limit, so this is a fact and not work. Self-Observation raises the work (REQ-SO-020), and the agent that receives it is one that the limit does not stop (REQ-EX-024).

text: The system shall refuse each request that changes state at a service, from a session that an agent drives as a sequence of steps on a connection that states that its account can commit funds or communicate with a third party in the name of the user.
rationale: RSK-EX-001, DEC-105 and DEC-127. The system cannot tell what a step does, so it refuses by what the connection states and by whether the request changes state, which it can see. OPN-093 asks whether this holds on real services. OPN-081.

text: The system shall report a change in the description that a service gives of the operation that a call names.
rationale: RSK-EX-007 and DEC-139. The system sees the operation in each call, so it needs nothing from Actuation to find a change. It reports and carries the call.

text: The system shall give Ingestion each delivery that a service sends without a request on a connection that the definition of a source names.
rationale: DEC-032 and DEC-129. REQ-IN-004 is the other side. The answer to a consent is the system's own (REQ-EX-012).

text: The system shall refuse a delivery that it cannot confirm as sent by the service of a declared connection.
rationale: RSK-EX-011. The address that accepts a delivery is reachable by anyone.

text: The system shall give Self-Observation, for each call, the service, the system that called, the agent that the caller states where it states one, the time, the outcome, the usage and the cost, and not the content of the call.
rationale: DEC-169 holds the record of the act, and this record is of the call. The content is life data that State Custody holds, and a second copy of it is the failure that DEC-019 states. DEC-165 has this system compute the cost, which the limit needs, sums the cost of the month from the records for the limit, and gives that sum to Self-Observation (DEC-165), so the cost is computed in one place. OPN-099: the agent is in the record because the bounds of cost are for each agent (DEC-145) and an agent that reads the records finds the cost of each agent.

text: The system shall accept a copy only from State Custody, Agent Definition, Authorization, Actuation and Ingestion.
rationale: DEC-020, DEC-123, DEC-128 and DEC-157. INT-PL-07, INT-PL-13 and INT-PL-58, and the rows of Actuation and Ingestion. REQ-EX-038 carries it.

text: The system shall give a holder, for a restoration, a copy that the holder gave.
rationale: DEC-128. REQ-ST-020, REQ-ST-071, REQ-AD-037, REQ-AU-016, REQ-AC-044 and REQ-IN-043 restore from it.

text: The system shall hold each copy away from the host in a form that nobody can read without its key.
rationale: RSK-EX-006 and DEC-128. REQ-ST-021 holds when the user reads the copy with the key.

text: The system shall not keep a copy away from the host for longer than TBD days.
rationale: RSK-EX-003 and DEC-128. A removal is complete when the last copy made before it is gone.

text: The system shall report a copy that a holder gave and that it did not carry within TBD.
rationale: RSK-EX-010. A restoration test restores the last copy that arrived, so a copy that did not arrive is not found by REQ-ST-025.

text: The system shall hold, with each connection, the time at which the user gave its credential.
rationale: DEC-125 makes the consent of the user at the service the answer to the connection, and REQ-PL-030 records an answer of the user as the platform received it.

text: The system shall give the declared connections and the content of each.
rationale: An agent names a connection in a source or an act and proposes its removal, and the user sees what access the platform holds. REQ-IN-002 states the same for sources. REQ-EX-016 keeps the credential out of it.

text: The system shall carry each copy that it accepts to the location away from the host.
rationale: DEC-020 and DEC-128. Rule 1 separates it from REQ-EX-031, which states who may give a copy.

text: The system shall refuse the removal of a connection that a declared act or the definition of a source names.
rationale: DEC-071 and DEC-125. An act or a source that names a removed connection fails at each call and nothing says why. REQ-AC-003 and REQ-IN-027 state the same.

text: The system shall accept from Agent Definition the cost of the use of each model.
rationale: DEC-165. The cost of a call to a model is its usage at the cost that Agent Definition holds (REQ-AD-044). The cost of another metered service is what its connection states (REQ-EX-043).

text: The system shall refuse a call to a model that gives the model a tool which the connection of the model provider does not name as one that only reads or as one that reaches no external service.
rationale: DEC-160. The model provider can run a tool for a call, and the call states each tool that it gives, so this system sees each one because it carries the call. A tool that acts would act at a service with no Actuation and no answer of the user. Whether a tool reaches out of the provider cannot be seen in the call, so the system refuses by what the connection names and not by what a tool does, as REQ-EX-026 does.

text: The system shall not accept the declaration of a connection, or a change to a connection, that names a tool as one that only reads or as one that reaches no external service, until the platform records an affirmative answer to a request that states that tool.
rationale: RSK-EX-018. To name a tool lets it pass REQ-EX-041, which makes a gate weaker, and DEC-113 has the user answer that. The shape of REQ-EX-006. DEC-160.

text: The system shall refuse a call to a metered connection when neither Agent Definition nor the connection states the cost of that call.
rationale: DEC-165. The limit needs the cost of each call. Agent Definition holds the cost of the model of an agent (REQ-EX-040), and the connection states the cost of any other call, including a call to a model that no agent names (DEC-154). Whether a connection will serve such a call is not known when it is declared, so the cost is checked at the call.

text: The system shall give, with the work that it raises for a connection that has no valid credential, the consent that it started for that connection, where the service offers one.
rationale: DEC-168 has the raiser state what it supplies. REQ-EX-012 accepts a credential in answer to a consent that the system started, so the work carries that consent to the agent that tells the user. What the agent tells the user is agent behaviour.

text: The system shall refuse a call to a model from a system other than Agent Runtime when the call names an operation that the connection of the provider does not name as one that does not generate.
rationale: DEC-154 and DEC-153. A provider gives generation and the other uses of a model as different operations, and a call names the one that it asks for, so this system refuses by a lookup and not by a judgement of the call. The shape of REQ-EX-041. Every call to a model reaches this system (DEC-161). Unlike a tool (REQ-EX-042), naming such an operation needs no answer of the user, because only the three systems of DEC-154, whose calls are fixed, call through it and no agent does (REQ-EX-020).

text: The system shall give Self-Observation each fact that it reports.
rationale: DEC-162. The facts are those of REQ-EX-025, REQ-EX-027 and REQ-EX-035. INT-PL-115.

text: The system shall give Self-Observation the metered cost of the current month that it sums for the limit, and the limit.
rationale: DEC-165. Self-Observation reports this sum and does not make a second sum of one cost (DEC-019). INT-PL-120.
